visual_summary: A two-story modern minimalist residential villa characterized by a large, cantilevered rectangular upper volume over a recessed ground floor entrance and carport area.

massing.overall_form: Rectangular prism cantilevered over a void-heavy ground floor podium.
volume_relationships: Upper floor projects forward to create a covered space below
Ground floor is partially recessed into the building footprint
massing.cantilever_or_projection: Major front-facing cantilever over the carport area.

facade_elements.description: Solid monolithic surface with dot texture representing fair-faced concrete tie-rod holes.

facade_elements.location: Ground floor carport and entry walls
facade_elements.description: Repetitive horizontal lines suggesting timber or metal cladding.

openings.description: Large single-pane window set deep into the upper facade volume.
Entrance door integrated into the horizontal slatted wall pattern.
Wide, unobstructed opening for vehicle access under the cantilever.

site_elements.description: Low-profile rectangular planter along the pedestrian path.
Organic bush/shrub forms at the site edges.
Ground plane treatment leading to the carport and entrance.

material_cues.evidence: Regular dot patterns across the rectangular facade.

generation_constraints: Maintain the structural cantilever of the second floor over the ground floor carport.
The depth of the upper floor window recess must be consistent with the massing depth.
Align the horizontal slat spacing across the ground floor walls and entrance door for a seamless look.
Ensure recessed ceiling lights (soffit lighting) are placed under the cantilevered volume.
clarification_questions: Is the upper facade intended to be fair-faced concrete or stone cladding?
Should the garage area include a garage door, or remain an open carport as sketched?
What is the required floor-to-ceiling height for the ground floor?
Are the ceiling dots under the cantilever intended to be recessed spotlights?
